title: fix(cluster)!: a Redis outage must not crash replicas; resync caches on reconnect (#3814 F3a)
body:
epic:#3814#1 · os-zhuang · session_01QUs3BrVu5TqwtmuhsjdEvM
Filing gate: ③ maintainer-dispatched task (child of #3814). Maintainer, (2026-11-08, 16:25 UTC): 「继续，现在派第二批」 (gate 1 after the card 0 inventory, cloud#3868 comment 6723322368).

Parent: #3814 (rulings R0-R6 on comment 6722625146).

## Problem (reproduced on the EE image by card 0)
With 2 replicas on the Redis cluster driver, stopping Redis made **every** replica exit 1 at its next 5-minute `approvals-sla-escalation` tick (r1 at +7 s, r2 at +114 s). Cause: the cron leader lock (`service-job` `cron-job-adapter.ts`, cluster lock `job:<name>`) calls `acquire` on the Redis driver, which throws `MaxRetriesPerRequestError` (ioredis lazyConnect, maxRetriesPerRequest 3); the fire runs as `void runScheduled(...)`, so the rejection is unhandled and the process dies. ioredis also logs `Unhandled error event` because `service-cluster-redis` attaches no `error` listener. Separately, a metadata publish during a 16 s blip was caught and logged (`metadata-manager.ts:3325`) and the event was **lost**: ioredis resubscribed all 4 lanes, but nothing resyncs what was missed. Until this lands, "Redis required" makes Redis a cluster-wide single point of failure.

## Do
1. A lock acquire/release failure skips that fire with one warning per outage (not per tick) and never rejects unhandled; the next tick tries again. Cover every cluster-lock caller on the EE boot path (cron, DbJobAdapter, anything else card 0 lists).
2. `service-cluster-redis`: attach `error` listeners on every client (command + subscriber) and log once per outage with no credential in the line; expose driver health for the readiness card.
3. On reconnect, emit one local "cluster resync" event; metadata, datasource, connector-credential and authz caches (and the settings/registry caches once their lanes exist) flush or re-read on it, so a publish lost during the blip converges.
4. No process-wide `unhandledRejection` swallow: fix the callers. A last-resort logger is acceptable only if it does not change single-node crash semantics.
5. Tests: a Redis driver stopped and restarted under a running kernel (real Redis or the driver's own fault seam): no exit, one warning, the next fire after reconnect runs, a publish during the outage reaches the peer after reconnect.

## Rules that bind every #3814 child (verbatim rulings on the parent)
R1 peer round-robin. R2 Redis required for multi-replica only. R3 「同意：每张卡都只在"声明多副本并接上 Redis 驱动"时才生效」: the single-node default path is unchanged, multi-replica behaviour switches on only behind declared replicas>1 AND a connected Redis cluster driver, the split-brain guard is never weakened, and the deploy README "multi-node unsupported" line stays until the final gate.

## Done when
PR merged; with Redis stopped, replicas keep serving DB-backed requests and stay up; after Redis returns, scheduled work resumes and caches converge without a restart; single node (memory driver) unchanged.

## Reader
Dispatched by the #3814 PM thread to one card thread; reviewed and landed by that PM thread. Priority p1: on the HA critical path.
